why: Story 7.0: verify PROVISIONS Playwright when the compiled plan carries a browser probe. This embodies no defect class from brief section 7 -- it is the proof for a capability that was written in story 5.1, unit-tested, documented in two user-facing messages, and called from nowhere in src/ for the whole of Epics 5 and 6 (D-5 of the first dogfooding run, docs/findings/dogfooding-defects-2026-09-05.md). Structurally the same defect story 6.11 closed for setup.install, and it survived for the same reason: the only tests that exercised provisioning called it themselves. THE FIXTURE IS BUILT SO THAT THE CODE IT REPLACED WOULD FAIL IT. Before the change verify only RESOLVED the environment, found it absent, and the probes stage refused with 'browser probe for E7-01 cannot run: @playwright/test does not resolve from ... and is not in the SpecWitness cache' -- an accurate classification (exit 3, never FAIL) reached without one byte of provisioning ever being attempted, which is exactly what the corpus could not previously see. After the change the same line reads 'cannot run: installing @playwright/test into <cache> failed' -- the run decided from the PLAN that a browser was needed, called provisionPlaywright, and the corpus's own npm tripwire refused the fetch. The two messages differ in the one word that matters: RESOLVING versus INSTALLING. WHY THE RUN STILL REACHES THE PROBES STAGE rather than ending at the CLI edge: a provisioning failure is carried into the environment the executor refuses on, so the pipeline runs and writes result.json. Throwing at the edge would end the command before the persist stage, and on the one path where verify may spend provider quota -- no plan on disk, so one is compiled first -- the run would have printed 'its provider usage is recorded in the run document' and then written no document at all. That is FR-18 auditability, and it is why exitCode 3 here comes with a real run document rather than with empty stdout. WHY THE FIXTURE CANNOT SIMPLY LET IT DOWNLOAD: an npm install plus a chromium bundle is hundreds of megabytes from two public origins, and tooth 2 of the runner's hermeticity contract says no fixture fetches anything. The tripwire is how that promise survives a product that can now fetch on its own -- see writeRegistryTripwires in tests/corpus/runner.ts. What is NOT pinned here, because no hermetic fixture can pin it, is that a real provisioning SUCCEEDS; that is tests/provisioning/playwright.provision.ts, which runs against the real registry, opt-in.
